title: Inside the cost-effectiveness model
html:
Where do figures like “$3,000–5,000 per life saved” come from? Behind each GiveWell recommendation is a spreadsheet that sets out every assumption and calculation. In the workbook you will open one.

Two terms in the reading are worth knowing beforehand:

  • Benchmark. GiveWell’s reference point is the value of giving cash to people in poverty in low-income countries, counting only the increase in what they can buy. It states every programme as a multiple of that: “10x our benchmark” means ten times as much good per dollar.

  • Funding bar. The multiple a programme usually has to reach before GiveWell funds it. As of May 2026 it is 6x the benchmark, and it moves with how much funding GiveWell expects to have. This is the same idea as Coefficient Giving’s bar from Week 1.

Read: GiveWell, How we use cost-effectiveness estimates (5 mins).
